<!-- DRAFT — general-lesson spin-off from the anomaly-detection project. -->

A detector that cries wolf gets ignored, and an ignored detector is worthless no matter its recall. The fix is usually less about a fancier model and more about modeling correlation — and making each alert explainable enough to act on.

## Why per-signal thresholds over-fire

\<Correlated signals move together; single-variable thresholds flag normal joint motion.\>

## Explainability is adoption

\<SHAP-per-alert mattered as much as the score for ops trust.\>

## Takeaway

Optimize false positives at fixed recall, and ship explanations with every alert.
